elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 18.3 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed by and construed and enforced under New York law.

elements.element: The state and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over disputes arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 17.3(a) grants those courts exclusive jurisdiction only over the merits of a defined “Dispute.” Expert matters and inventorship disputes are excluded from that definition, and either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction. The required exclusive New York County forum is therefore not comprehensive.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware law, California law, or the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 18.3 selects New York law, not any permitted fallback law.

elements.element: The court forum corresponds to the selected fallback law: Delaware courts, California courts, or, for the laws of England and Wales, the courts of London.
elements.evidence: Section 17.3(a) selects courts located in New York County, subject to exceptions, rather than any permitted fallback court forum.

result.reason: The New York governing-law requirement is met, but the jurisdiction provision is narrower than the preferred position because it excludes certain dispute categories and permits temporary-injunction proceedings in any competent court. No fallback law or forum is selected. The redline generally preserves unrelated terms and expressly disables the residual arbitration provisions, but retaining the inapplicable arbitration language in Section 17.3(g) creates avoidable clutter, and the added forum exceptions prevent completion of the preferred position.
